props.heading: What is on the floor
props.intro: One big room on the ground floor, open to the street, with the shutters up in summer.

items.title: Six racks and platforms
items.text: Calibrated plates, bumpers and three women’s bars. Deadlift on the platforms, not on the tiles.

items.title: Dumbbells to 50 kg
items.text: In 2.5 kg steps, on two racks by the wall.

items.title: Kettlebells, 8 to 32 kg
items.text: Enough pairs for a full class of twelve.

items.title: Rowers and air bikes
items.text: Four of each, for warm-ups and the Friday conditioning class.

items.title: Boxing corner
items.text: Three heavy bags, pads and gloves you can borrow.

items.title: Showers that work
items.text: Hot water all year, lockers, and a separate women’s changing room.

image.alt: A lifter setting up for a deadlift on the rubber floor

items.title: Strength classes
items.text: Squat, bench, deadlift and press, in groups of eight with one coach. You follow a written programme, and the coach sets your weights from last week’s log.

image.alt: Rows of black kettlebells ready for the conditioning class

items.title: Conditioning
items.text: Forty minutes of kettlebells, rowers and carries. Hard, short and over before you can think about it. Scaled for every level.

image.alt: A coach correcting a man’s push-up position on the turf

items.title: One-to-one coaching
items.text: For a first-timer, a comeback after injury or a meet. Your own programme, checked every session, with a written plan to take home.

props.quote: Most people who walk in here have been told they are doing it wrong. We would rather show them how to do it right, one rep at a time.
props.name: Kiran Thapa

props.heading: Your first four weeks
props.intro: Everyone starts the same way, whether you have lifted for years or never touched a bar.

image.alt: A member doing a split squat with a barbell in a squat rack

items.label: Week 1
items.title: Assessment
items.text: Thirty minutes with a coach: old injuries, how you move, what you want. We film a squat and a hinge so you can see where you start.

items.label: Week 2
items.title: The basic lifts
items.text: Squat, hinge, push and pull with a bar or a kettlebell. Light weights, many small corrections.

items.label: Week 3
items.title: Your programme
items.text: A written three-day plan, logged in a notebook we keep at the desk. Weights go up only when the coach says the form is ready.

items.label: Week 4
items.title: Retest
items.text: The same film as week one, side by side. Then you choose a membership, or you do not. No hard sell.

props.heading: The floor at six in the morning
props.intro: Busiest from 6:00 to 8:00 and 17:30 to 19:30. Quietest at noon.

props.heading: Coached by people who lift
props.body:
Kiran has coached strength for eleven years and competes in powerlifting. The three coaches with him are all certified, first-aid trained and on the floor, not behind the desk.

There is always a coach on the floor. If you are unsure about a lift, ask; that is what they are there for.

items.q: I have never lifted. Is that a problem?
items.a: No. About half our members had not held a barbell before they came. Everyone starts with the same four weeks.
Women’s Strength runs Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday at 7:00 with a woman coach, and there is a separate women’s changing room with its own shower.
Flat shoes or clean trainers, a water bottle and a towel. We lend belts, wraps and gloves.
Three-month and yearly members can freeze for travel, exams or injury. Tell the desk a day before.
Cash, card, eSewa, Khalti or Fonepay QR at the desk. We give a VAT bill for every payment.

props.title: Your first class is on us
props.text: Pick a class and a time. Wear flat shoes, come ten minutes early, and meet the coach.

props.heading: How we coach
props.body:
Every member has a logbook at the desk. Coaches read it before your session, so nobody has to remember what you lifted last Tuesday.

We teach the lifts in the same order to everyone: hinge, squat, push, pull, carry. We do not sell supplements, and we will not tell you to buy any.

  • One coach for every eight people in a class
  • Form checked on the first working set of every lift
  • A retest every twelve weeks, on film
